Explain how a float valve keeps a livestock water trough filled, what happens as the water level rises, and two ordinary causes of overflow. Use plain accurate prose. Aim for approximately 120–170 English tokens.

message.content: A float valve controls trough filling by using a buoyant float connected to a valve. When the water level drops, the float sinks and opens the valve, letting water in. As the water rises, the float rises with it and gradually closes the valve. At the set level, the valve shuts off and filling stops. Two ordinary causes of overflow are debris or mineral buildup preventing the valve from closing fully, and a misadjusted float set too high so the valve closes only after the trough is already overflowing.
